page.layout: One page of running text, single column, no margin notes. Printed page number at the head, centred. Catchword at the lower right. Faint show-through of the reverse page is ignored.

main_text.l: Cum autem noticiæ sint gubernatrices actio-
num, Aristoteles optimo ordine adiungit parti-
tionibus iusticiæ sapientissimam distinctionem
legum naturæ & iuris positivi, quia iustitia
in hominibus est velle & imperare membris con-
formia legi.
XIX.
Ac leges quidem naturæ sunt noticiæ prin-
cipiorum practicorum, & conclusionum ex
his extructarum de regendis moribus, congruentes
cum æterna & immota norma mentis divinæ,
insitæ nobis divinitus, ut sint testimonia, quod
sit Deus, & qualis sit, & regant nos, ut congruat
obedientia nostra cum voluntate Dei.
XX.
Ius vero positivum est decretum legitimæ po-
testatis, non pugnans cum iure naturæ, sed ad-
dens ad ius naturæ circumstantiam aliquam pro-
babili ratione, non necessario definitam.
XXI.
Sed inter ius naturæ, & ius positivum
hoc interest, quod cum ius naturæ loquatur de gener-
e, & habeat suas demonstrationes, & ubique
sit idem, & neq; tolli neq; abrogari possit, ius posi-
tivum loquitur de specie, & ratum est partim
propter autoritatem legislatoris, partim propter
probabilem rationem,
nec ubiq; idem est, deniq;[?] mutari & solet & potest.

page.notes: Page number XVIII is at the head, centred, printed in roman numerals. No running head is printed. The catchword "Discer-" is at the lower right. The signature "A 3" at the foot is faint and partly overlaid by show-through, so it is doubtful. "deniq;" is uncertain in the scan and is marked. Roman numerals XIX, XX and XXI are bare numbers set as paragraph openers, so they are written as paragraphs. Printed spelling kept: "autoritatem", "iusticiæ", "noticiæ", "divinitus".
